headline: Residue networks and sequence tools probe allostery, repeats, and Fe-S protein features
label: Protein Structure Bioinformatics Methods
summary: Allostery is now linked to loss-of-function variant pathogenicity, alongside new tools for directional residue networks and protein sequence databases.
synthesis: The items share a computational emphasis on resolving residue-level and sequence-level determinants of protein behavior. TEntroPy applies transfer entropy to MD trajectories to build directional residue networks that map allosteric information flow. A published framework separates allosteric disruption from destabilization and proposes that allostery is a widespread cause of loss-of-function variant pathogenicity. Contact-Network Responsiveness scores how structure-derived contact networks respond to strengthened or weakened contacts across human proteins. On the sequence side, Drepper quantifies repeat complexity and reveals lineage-specific repeat architectures in protozoan proteomes, and FeSseqdb pairs a PDB-derived, atomically verified Fe-S sequence database with an interpretable random forest classifier. A Gompertz fit to PDB depositions and cumulative novel folds projects future entry and fold counts. The pathogen-relevant element is limited to the protozoan repeat survey; the common thread is methodological rather than pathogen genome-specific.
